profile.hobby: restoring a red 1972 Olivetti Valentine typewriter

memories.text: Walked the Pier 48 floor with the event crew and measured the demo table at 180 centimetres, which is 20 short of what the projector throw needed.
Decided to hold the speaker embeddings at 256 dimensions instead of going to 512, because the extra 256 bought us nothing on the eight-voice test set.
My sister Nadia called from Lisbon at lunchtime to argue that the product name sounds like a password manager, and I told her that was exactly the point.
Finally found a ribbon spool that fits the red Olivetti Valentine typewriter I bought at the Alameda flea market, and the letter e still prints half a shade light.
Ran four sets of the Dolores Park stairs before work and had to stop on the third because a loose dog decided to run them with me.
Cut the onboarding flow from five screens down to two and moved the permission prompt to after the first success instead of before it.
The barista at Ruby's on Minnesota Street told me they are discontinuing the cold brew in September, and I asked her to save me the last keg.
We are six people now that Priya started, and she is the only one who has ever shipped a vector index in production before.
Got to the Ferry Building farmers market at half past noon and the Blenheim apricots were already gone, so I bought two pounds of Santa Rosa plums instead.
Locked the demo script to exactly three beats and threw out the fourth one about audit logs because it added ninety seconds and no drama.
At standup we admitted recall had been stuck at 61 percent for three straight days and nobody had a theory that survived five minutes of questions.
Spent twenty minutes on the phone with our advisor Marcus who insisted the entropy meter should count down in bits rather than show a percentage.
Decided the projector shows only the entropy number and the candidate bars, and that every log line goes to a second screen the audience never sees.
Decided to switch the retriever from plain BM25 to hybrid rankFusion after the recall numbers stalled at 61 percent.
Told you about the burnt espresso at the Dogpatch cafe next to the pier, and that I switched to their cold brew instead.
Packed the demo bag last night with two USB-C to HDMI adapters, a thirty foot extension cord, and the lapel mic that always drops its left channel.
Missed the 8:52 T train because the Third Street signal was down, so I walked twenty minutes and arrived late to standup.
My sister Nadia is flying in from Lisbon on the 22nd and staying through Labor Day weekend.
